questions.prompt: Audit logs are written once and read maybe twice a year, but must be retrievable within milliseconds when needed. Which storage class fits best?

options.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering with archive tiers enabled

questions.explanation: Standard-IA suits rarely accessed data that still needs immediate access. Deep Archive is cheaper but retrieval takes hours, which breaks the millisecond requirement.

questions.prompt: What happens when you delete an object in a versioning-enabled bucket without specifying a version ID?

options.text: A delete marker is added and older versions remain
The request fails until versioning is suspended
The latest version moves to Glacier

questions.explanation: A simple delete adds a delete marker that hides the object; earlier versions stay and can be restored. Permanent removal requires deleting specific version IDs.

questions.prompt: Which actions can an S3 lifecycle rule perform? Select two.

options.text: Encrypt existing objects with a new KMS key
Transition objects to a cheaper storage class

questions.explanation: Lifecycle rules transition, expire, and clean up incomplete multipart uploads. Re-encryption and cross-region copies are handled by other features such as Batch Operations and replication.

questions.prompt: A team needs to control who can use the encryption key for a bucket and see key usage in CloudTrail. Which default encryption option fits?

options.text: No encryption, rely on Block Public Access

questions.explanation: SSE-KMS lets you control key permissions with key policies and logs key use in CloudTrail. SSE-S3 encrypts data but gives you no key-level control or audit trail.
